The note indicates that because Bentham's calculus treats pleasure and pain as the fundamental units of value, the strongest refutation is the argument that these experiences are inevitable features of life rather than solely dependent on individual choice. This objection challenges the core assumption that one can simply maximize or minimize such states without acknowledging their inescapable nature in human existence. Consequently, this perspective undermines the practical applicability and theoretical completeness of a system built entirely upon quantifying pleasure and pain.
